p5-s6: In my land there is a wide river, and across the river there is a bridge.
p5-s7: Right at the entrance, before the bridge begins, there are two guards and a jail.
p5-s8: The owner of the bridge made a law: whoever arrives tells the guards where he is going.
p5-s9: Whoever tells the truth crosses the bridge.
p5-s10: Whoever lies doesn’t cross: he goes straight to jail, right there beside it.
p5-s14: One would say I’m going to the market and cross.
p5-s15: Another would say I’m going to visit my granny and cross as well.
p5-s16: Then, yesterday, a man arrived, and the guards asked him, as always: Where are you going?.
p5-s17: And he answered, very calmly: I am going to jail.
p5-s19: If they let the man cross the bridge, he wasn’t going to jail: so he had lied... and whoever lies doesn’t cross, he goes to jail!
p5-s20: But if they put the man in jail, he really was going where he said: so he had told the truth... and whoever tells the truth has to cross!
p5-s21: Lock him up, let him go, lock him up, let him go...
